claims.text: Tribo-corrosion degradation in high-entropy alloys is governed by the dynamic interaction between passive-film removal and film reformation.
Sliding wear continuously removes the protective passive oxide film faster than it can reform.
Removal of the passive film exposes fresh metal that corrodes more aggressively.
Corrosion further disrupts the passive-film structure and reduces its protection against wear.
The proposed high-entropy alloy is homogeneous and passivating.
The alloy naturally develops a protective oxide layer under ambient conditions.
Passive-film integrity and repassivation kinetics at the wear interface mediate the coupled response.
When passive-film removal outpaces repassivation, the continuously exposed substrate undergoes accelerated corrosion.
Corrosion damage degrades the mechanical properties of the near-surface region.
Corrosion-induced degradation of the near-surface region accelerates wear, producing a synergistic cycle.
Total degradation under combined tribo-corrosion will exceed the sum of degradation under wear-only and corrosion-only conditions.
Combined tribo-corrosion will produce greater mass loss or wear-track volume than the matched individual conditions.
Combined tribo-corrosion will increase localized pit formation.
Combined tribo-corrosion will cause more extensive surface damage.
Synergistic degradation should occur when repassivation kinetics are too slow to keep pace with wear-induced film removal.
Rapid passive-film reformation can minimize the coupling effect.
A very low wear rate can prevent the predicted synergistic degradation from manifesting.
The magnitude of synergy depends on alloy-specific repassivation kinetics, local wear intensity, and corrosive severity.
